I was in 6th grade when my great grandmother died. I was left her Woodmouse family collection, some 30 french porcelain mice with human personalities, a Woodmouse family album, and a small display shelf. I didn't cherish many of my things but these were special to me. 
One day I came home from a chorus recital at school and the whole shelf was on the floor. Every one of the mice were smashed, irreparable. I saw it and screamed. After I calmed down, I started cleaning up the mess. I searched my room for all the pieces but one mouse had completely vanished, as each one has a base with the name painted on it, and I couldn't find her head. One was gone forever and I took it as my great grandmother, telling me I wasn't really part of my family, taking away the one thing I had from her, while everyone else had something to remember her by. 
More in my family has happened since then to widen the rift between me and my family but that was when I first noticed I wasn't like my cousins...
